name: Relative Error
description: Learn about Relative Error and its applications in physics.

content.overview: Here's a puzzle: being off by 1 cm sounds small... unless you were only measuring a 2 cm paperclip. Being off by 1 cm on a 100-meter running track? Basically nothing. Relative error is what lets you compare those two situations fairly. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Relative error = absolute error ÷ true value {{viz:diagram-02}}
It's a fraction (no units!)—it strips away scale so errors become comparable
A 1 cm error is huge relative to a 2 cm paperclip, but tiny relative to a 100 m track
Multiply relative error by 100 and you get percentage error (up next)
content.whyItMatters: Relative error is what lets scientists and engineers say whether an error actually matters. A tiny absolute error can be a big deal on a small measurement, and a big absolute error can be irrelevant on a huge one. Relative error puts every measurement on the same fair footing.
